source.title: 3D-Mesh NRW (Geobasis NRW)
source.format: I3S (Indexed 3D Scene Layer), service version 1.7, meshpyramids/node-switching LOD
source.geometryEncoding: uncompressed (geometries/0) used; draco (geometries/1) also available but not needed
source.note: Same coordinate system BEUTELTIER already uses; no reprojection needed.

roi.describes: Halle 9, Halle 10, Boulevard, Piazza / Eingang Sued approach

changesFromV1: traverse.mjs: ROI-overlap test replaced bounding-sphere (over-inclusive in all directions by the OBB diagonal length) with a rotation-aware axis-aligned XY footprint test (xyFootprint() in i3s-transform.mjs, projects all 8 rotated OBB corners) -- still conservative for rotated boxes, but far tighter. The sphere test let large, elongated background nodes graze into the ROI from up to ~900m away and pulled in their entire real-world footprint.

traverse.mjs: added real gap detection (coversFootprint(), a 48x48 raster over each node's ROI-clipped footprint) -- when a node's matching children do not fully cover the node's own ROI-clipped area, the node itself is also kept (not just descended into), closing genuine local coverage holes instead of leaving them undetected.

traverse.mjs: gap-fill and the plain 'no matching children -> keep node' rule are both gated by eligibleForPick() (i3s-transform.mjs) -- a node above local-tile scale (halfSize x/y > 100m) is only kept if a real majority (>=30%) of its OWN footprint actually lies in the ROI. A node is a complete standalone mesh over its ENTIRE OBB, not just the ROI-overlapping sliver, so keeping a large node that only grazes the ROI edge was pulling in hundreds of meters of irrelevant background.

build.mjs: added geometryExceedsDeclaredObb() (i3s-transform.mjs) -- rejects a node if its actual parsed local vertex extent exceeds its own declared obb.halfSize by more than 3x on any axis. Found and confirmed on real data: some nodes' geometry buffer does not match their own OBB metadata (example: node 20371600, declared halfSize.y=40.0m, actual local Y vertex extent ~912m) -- a source data inconsistency, not a transform bug (independently confirmed by rendering a known-good identity-quaternion leaf node, whose GLTFLoader-computed bounding box matched the independently-computed expected box exactly). 76/473 picked nodes (16%) failed this check for this ROI and were excluded rather than importing corrupted geometry.

New tools/nrw-mesh/i3s-transform.mjs: shared transform/parsing/geometry-validation module, imported by traverse.mjs, build.mjs and the new verify-single-node.mjs, so the single-node proof and the batch build are guaranteed to run identical logic.

New tools/nrw-mesh/verify-single-node.mjs: automated, reproducible single-leaf-node proof (geometry/UV/texture presence + independently cross-checked EPSG:25832->scene transform bounds), plus a standalone three.js/Playwright GLB viewer (tools external to the repo, see reproduceWith) with an automated non-blank-pixel check.

localArtifact.format: GLB (glTF 2.0 binary), one mesh+material+JPEG texture per source node

archivedNodeList.note: Committed (218KB, plain node metadata JSON, not a binary asset) so the exact 473-node ROI pick is reproducible without re-traversing the SceneServer -- pass it directly to build.mjs.

knownLimitation: Small residual local gaps can still remain at the very finest LOD where even a gap-filled node's own footprint doesn't fully cover its ROI-clipped area at leaf scale, and 76 nodes were deliberately excluded for failing the OBB/geometry consistency check (see nodesRejectedForObbGeometryMismatch) rather than importing corrupted geometry -- both are visible as small dark gaps in the rendered screenshot. The systemic issues from pipeline v1 (sphere over-inclusion pulling in far-away background, and undetected coverage holes) are fixed; see changesFromV1.

evaluatedPerUserRequest.result: FAILS. Connects to the real SceneServer, converts the root node (index 0) successfully, then crashes converting the next node with "TypeError: Cannot read properties of undefined (reading (quote)0(quote))" inside buildGLTF/_normalizePositions. Deterministic: reproduced identically with and without --no-draco. No CLI flag exists to scope the conversion to a bounding box/ROI, so even a working run would require converting arbitrary amounts of unrelated state before reaching Koeln.
evaluatedPerUserRequest.corroboration: Same undefined-property crash signature already reported against this tool for other I3S sources (visgl/loaders.gl issue #1734 and others) -- an existing, known-fragile code path, not specific to this dataset.
evaluatedPerUserRequest.conclusion: Not usable as-is for this task.

evaluatedPerUserRequest.result: Confirmed via the project README: no native I3S/Esri/SceneServer/Integrated-Mesh loader or plugin exists. It renders OGC 3D Tiles only, so it is entirely dependent on a working I3S-to-3D-Tiles conversion step, which is the broken step above.
evaluatedPerUserRequest.conclusion: Not applicable until an I3S source exists as valid 3D Tiles -- which tile-converter could not produce for this service.

evaluatedPerUserRequest.command: Standalone local proof (not part of the app): a static page loads Cesium.js, calls Cesium.I3SDataProvider.fromUrl('.../SceneServer') against the real NRW SceneServer (via a same-origin relay - this sandbox's headless Chromium cannot reach the public internet directly at all, confirmed with example.com too, unrelated to NRW; the relay just forwards the real bytes with plain Node fetch, which can reach it), then flies the camera to Koelnmesse.
evaluatedPerUserRequest.result: FAILS immediately and deterministically with 'RuntimeError: Unsupported spatial reference: 25832'. Confirmed by reading Cesium 1.144.0's own shipped source: I3SLayer.load() contains an unconditional `if (this._data.spatialReference.wkid !== 4326) throw ...` for I3S IntegratedMesh (3D mesh) layers - there is no reprojection path, no proj4/projection-engine hook, no option to override. The real NRW SceneServer publishes its mesh natively in EPSG:25832 (ETRS89/UTM32), which is common for national mapping agencies and is the same CRS BEUTELTIER's own pipeline already uses. Screenshot evidence: an unstyled Cesium globe with the exact error text overlaid, no NRW geometry loaded.
evaluatedPerUserRequest.corroboration: Independently corroborated by CesiumGS/cesium community reports (e.g. 'Cesium only supports EPSG:3857 and EPSG:4326' threads, UTM-georeferenced-model import issues) describing the same general projected-CRS limitation outside the I3S code path.
evaluatedPerUserRequest.conclusion: Not usable as-is for this task: this is a hard, unconditional code restriction in Cesium's I3S support, not a bug to retry around and not something to patch/fork per the explicit instruction not to modify third-party libraries during this task.

toolingEvaluation.chosenApproach: tools/nrw-mesh/traverse.mjs + build.mjs: parse the I3S REST responses directly (node pages, uncompressed geometry buffer, JPEG textures) and assemble one glTF with @gltf-transform/core. Verified working end-to-end against the same service these two tools failed on: 375/375 nodes fetched, real texture and geometry confirmed by rendering the output GLB with three.js under Playwright. CesiumJS I3SDataProvider was also evaluated directly against the real SceneServer per explicit request and rejected for the same reason: it only accepts I3S mesh layers published in EPSG:4326, and this service is EPSG:25832.
